relations.rationale: Checking the registration table is unrelated to where Tess stood in the pack.
Checking the registration table twice has no bearing on the crowd surging at the horn.
Making sure runners signed waivers plausibly involves checking a clipboard with names, supporting the claim Quinn glanced at one.
Quinn's waiver-checking activity is unrelated to when Uma arrived.
Ensuring waivers were signed before the race has no logical connection to laughter echoing at the finish area later.
Dara being in the same study group as Rosa doesn't determine whether Rosa is in the same group as Tess.

If Dara is in the same group as Rosa, and study groups are typically singular, this suggests Dara and Tess could differ only if Rosa and Tess differ, but the claim doesn't state that; still, transitively if Dara=Rosa's group, and Tess were in that group too, Dara would be in Tess's group, so this makes 'not same group' plausible only weakly.
Study group membership is unrelated to Dara's physical state after finishing a race.
The sun breaking through clouds at the five-minute warning is a natural/timing event unrelated to runners moving to corrals, though both occur near race start, they aren't causally linked.
Everyone moving toward corrals doesn't inform when Uma arrived earlier that day.
Moving toward corrals is a precursor to the crowd surging forward at the horn, supporting that sequence of events.
Moving toward corrals before the race is unrelated to Dara's emotional/physical state after finishing.

If Rosa is in the same study group as Tess, and study groups are typically singular per person, then Dara being in a different group from Tess is only consistent if Dara is also not in Rosa's group, creating tension with claim 11 but not directly contradicting 19 itself.
Study group membership between Rosa and Tess has no bearing on race finishing order.
Rosa and Tess's study group relationship is unrelated to Dara's post-race demeanor.
Study group membership is unrelated to ambient laughter at the finish area.
Quinn glancing at a clipboard is unrelated to laughter echoing at the finish area.
Uma's early arrival has no bearing on the rhythmic sound of sneakers on pavement.
Uma's early arrival time is unrelated to Dara crossing the finish line after Tess.
Arriving earlier than most participants doesn't directly imply or contradict finishing in the middle of the pack, since arrival time and finish position aren't necessarily linked.
